mechanism: Valproic acid inhibits glucuronidation and may increase mycophenolate levels, while mycophenolate's active metabolite (MPA) may displace valproic acid from protein binding, potentially increasing valproic acid concentrations.
action: Monitor valproic acid and mycophenolate levels; assess for signs of valproic acid toxicity (tremor, ataxia, lethargy) and mycophenolate toxicity (GI distress, bone marrow suppression); consider alternative immunosuppressants if toxicity occurs.
